🌿 When to plant scent leaf in Nigeria

Also called Nchanwu (Igbo), Efinrin (Yoruba) and Daidoya (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant scent leaf in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from all year round. Grown from seed or cuttings early in the rains; harvested all year.

PlantMarch to May
Harvestall year round

■ plant   ■ harvest

About scent leaf

Scent leaf (African basil) flavours pepper soup and many sauces.

How to plant scent leaf well

Pinch off flower heads to keep leaves tender.

Grown from seed or cuttings early in the rains; harvested all year.

Diseases and pests of scent leaf

  • AphidsSpray with water or neem extract.
  • Root rotAvoid waterlogged soil.

Best states for scent leaf

Enugu · Imo · Oyo · Delta · Edo

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant scent leaf in Nigeria?

Plant scent leaf in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from all year round. Grown from seed or cuttings early in the rains; harvested all year.

What is scent leaf called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Scent leaf is called Nchanwu (Igbo), Efinrin (Yoruba) and Daidoya (Hausa).

When is scent leaf harvested in Nigeria?

Scent leaf is usually harvested from all year round.

Which Nigerian states grow the most scent leaf?

Enugu, Imo, Oyo, Delta and Edo are among the best-known scent leaf states.

Can I grow scent leaf in my part of Nigeria?

Yes. Scent leaf grows in every region of Nigeria: North and South.

What diseases attack scent leaf and how do I prevent them?

Aphids: Spray with water or neem extract. Root rot: Avoid waterlogged soil.
